He ordered the executioners to be beheaded, and he dismissed the soldiers standing by him. He was angry and suspicious of his army, thinking a plot was being formed against him. He spoke to Saint Longinus, saying: 'Swear to me by the salvation of the gods that you will not speak or swear about the one born, or call him king, so that if you do this, you will escape the torments and punishments that await you.' Saint Longinus replied to the king, saying: 'By the glory of Jesus Christ, who saves those who believe in him, you will not persuade me to deny my God.' He trusted in God and was not afraid of the king's torments. Herod ordered him to be flogged. Saint Longinus was praising and saying: 'Lord, God, the eternal king of kings and lord of lords, who sits kings on the earth and lifts up the poor from the ground, the only merciful one, send your angel to strengthen me.' Herod, seeing that Saint Longinus did not feel the torments, said to his magistrates: 'Take him away to prison, bind him with chains, and after mocking him, bring him to me, so that I may reward you with great honor.' They took Saint Longinus with great sorrow to prison and did what they were ordered to do. After three days in prison, and with great distress for Herod because of the born king, Saint Longinus prayed at night, saying…

Lord Jesus Christ, send your angel and rescue your servants being punished here. And when he prayed, a great earthquake occurred, so that the prison was shaken, and light shone around holy Longinus, and a voice was heard saying to him: 'Rise quickly; for now is not the time to complete your martyrdom.' And immediately all the bonds fell off and the prison was opened and about a thousand men came out and fled from the city; and a great commotion occurred in the city. And the king heard what happened in the prison; and coming to the place and not finding holy Longinus there, he was perplexed about what happened. But holy Longinus was moving around in the city and no one could see him, because their eyes were darkened. Herod was searching for him; and there was a great commotion and loud noise in the city and they spoke against the pious. But Herod sent reminders to the nations, so that they might bring the holy Longinus as a prisoner, thinking that the servant of God had escaped from the city; for he was struck with blindness and lay down, and thus 'Herod, having become worm-eaten, died.' And Archelaus, the son of Herod, reigned in his place, having the same name as his father. But holy Longinus was in the holy city, waiting for salvation from God. And when Archelaus died, Herod, the brother of Philip, reigned over Judea and Galilee. And Longinus was received into his own order.

And he was beholding the great deeds of God and the wonders happening every day by our Lord Jesus Christ, until in the 15th year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, king of the Romans, and Herod, brother of Philip, through Herodias, beheaded John the Baptist, who also himself wickedly gave up the spirit and died. And Herod, son of Herod, brother of Archelaus, was reigning in Galilee. In the 25th year of his rule, on the 8th day before the Kalends of April, which is the 5th day of March, during the consulship of Rufus and Rubellius, in the 4th year of the second Olympiad, under the high priesthood of Joseph and Caiaphas, who also delivered our Lord Jesus Christ to Pilate to be crucified. But Pilate, knowing that Jesus was a Galilean and under Herod's authority, sent him to Herod, who was in Jerusalem. Herod, mocking and despising Jesus, clothed him in a bright robe and sent him back to Pilate. Pilate, calling together the chief priests and rulers, was examining them, saying that they had delivered an innocent man to him. But they all handed Jesus over to be crucified, and they crucified the one who bore the sin of the world, nailing him to the cross. For Pilate had handed Jesus over to the soldiers, and he appointed a centurion over them.
pass_b_english: The king, filled with anger and suspicion, ordered the executioners to be beheaded and dismissed the soldiers standing by him, thinking that a plot was being formed against him.

He then spoke to Saint Longinus, demanding that he swear by the salvation of the gods that he would not speak or swear about the one born, or call him king, in order to escape the torments and punishments that awaited him.
Saint Longinus refused, saying that he would not deny his God, trusting in Jesus Christ, who saves those who believe in him, and he was not afraid of the king's torments.

He praised God, saying, 'Lord, God, the eternal king of kings and lord of lords, who sits kings on the earth and lifts up the poor from the ground, the only merciful one, send your angel to strengthen me.'

Herod, seeing that Saint Longinus did not feel the torments, instructed his magistrates to take him away to prison, bind him with chains, and after mocking him, bring him to the king, so that he might reward them with great honor.
After three days in prison, Saint Longinus prayed at night, saying, 'Lord, Jesus Christ, send your angel and rescue your servants who are being punished here.'

As he prayed, a great earthquake struck, causing the prison to shake violently, and a light shone around holy Longinus, and a voice was heard, urging him to rise quickly, for it was not yet time to complete his martyrdom, saying, 'Rise quickly; for now is not the time to complete your martyrdom.'

Immediately, the bonds that held the prisoners fell away, and the prison doors swung open, and about a thousand men emerged and fled the city, creating a great commotion, and there was a great uproar in the city.

The king, upon hearing of the events in the prison, rushed to the scene, only to find that holy Longinus was nowhere to be found, leaving him perplexed, and he was searching for him, but holy Longinus was moving freely about the city, and no one could see him, for their eyes had been darkened.

Herod, determined to capture him, sent out search parties, but to no avail, and the city was in an uproar, with loud noises and angry voices raised against the pious, and he sent reminders to the nations, hoping to capture the servant of God, whom he believed had escaped from the city.
However, Herod's own life was soon to come to an end, for he was struck with blindness and lay dying, his body consumed by worms, and he eventually died.
Archelaus, the son of Herod, took his place as ruler, bearing the same name as his father.

Holy Longinus waited patiently in the holy city for salvation from God, and after the death of Archelaus, Herod, the brother of Philip, reigned over Judea and Galilee, and Longinus was received into his own order.
He was beholding the great deeds of God and the wonders happening every day by our Lord Jesus Christ.
In the 15th year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, king of the Romans, and Herod, brother of Philip, John the Baptist was beheaded through Herodias (Matthew 14:10).
Herod, son of Herod, brother of Archelaus, was reigning in Galilee.

In the 25th year of his rule, during the consulship of Rufus and Rubellius, under the high priesthood of Joseph and Caiaphas, our Lord Jesus Christ was delivered to Pilate to be crucified (Luke 23:1).
Pilate, knowing that Jesus was a Galilean and under Herod's authority, sent him to Herod, who was in Jerusalem.
Herod, mocking and despising Jesus, clothed him in a bright robe and sent him back to Pilate (Luke 23:11).
Pilate, calling together the chief priests and rulers, was examining them, saying that they had delivered an innocent man to him.
They handed Jesus over to be crucified, and they crucified the one who bore the sin of the world (John 1:29), nailing him to the cross.
Pilate appointed a centurion over the soldiers who crucified him.
